newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian wool growers get A$80 mln in WI wind up.
newsitem.headline: Australian wool growers get A$80 mln in WI wind up.

text.p: CANBERRA, June 26 - The Australian parliament on Thursday passed laws to wind up Wool International (WI) and give back at least A$80 million in levies to Australian wool growers this year.
The Wool International Amendment Bill 1997 establishes the procedures for dismantling of WI, the statutory body charged with selling off Australia's wool stockpile.
The new legislation allows for WI's liquidation and the distribution of the revenues to growers.
The growers paid a wool tax from 1993-1996 to help manage and dispose of the stockpile.
The sale of the stockpile, created in the last years of the Reserve Price Scheme, will pay off debts and any other profits will be distributed to wool tax payers.

"It is expected growers will receive their first distribution of equity in the wool stockpile by October, and overall this move will release hundreds of millions of dollars back to woolgrowers," Primary Industries Minister John Anderson said in a statement.
